result:
Extraction complete. Output written atomically to `corpus/silver/pilot_v6/fable51_high/1306.2128v2.json` after finalize passed with zero errors and zero warnings.

**Paper.** Bugeaud & Dujella, "Root separation for reducible integer polynomials" (2013). Four theorem environments, no proof environments: all four proofs, every definition, claim and remark are prose.

**Counts**

| | |
|---|---|
| Nodes | 110 (44 Level-1 + 66 proof_step) |
| By type | 15 definition, 9 theorem, 7 remark, 6 claim, 4 proof, 2 proposition, 1 corollary, 66 proof_step |
| Edges | 102 (97 uses, 4 proves, 1 specializes); 3 added by finalize from `\ref` |
| From environment facts vs prose | 4 vs 40 Level-1 nodes |
| External nodes | 10 (Mahler ×2, Evertse–Schönhage, four-paper bounds, BM1/BM2 cluster bounds, 4 imported definitions incl. Fibonacci) |
| Orphans | 1 (RP1.4, the implied-constants convention; nothing references it) |
| Mean confidence | nodes 0.74, edges 0.84 |
| statement_short coverage | 83% overall; 100% proofs and steps, 100% claims, 7/9 theorems, 7/15 definitions |
| rigor_nonformal_count | 6 (all semi_formal: "Obviously", "easy to check", "We deduce from (10)", sketch-proved claim, Theorem 4 and its "we omit the details" proof) |
| Backward edges | 3 (intro overview remark uses the S2 construction ×2; Mahler's cluster bound in S5 generalizes his S1 bound) |

**Steps per parent.** PP1.1: 12 (+2 nested under the claim (2)); PP1.2: 18; PP1.3: 20 (+2 under the monicity claim, +9 under the conjugate-roots claim); PP1.4: 3. Each proof's steps cover 100% of the parent body.

**Finalize.** 4 nodes matched to environments, 3 labels filled, 0 proves added by syntax (no proof environments, so I supplied all 4 proves edges), 3 `\ref` uses edges added, 0 backward refs, 0 unresolved refs.

**Spec ambiguities and judgment calls**
- Rule 7 claim terminators never match in this paper ("the claim follows by induction", a proof ending at "= 1." then a paragraph break). Applied literally, children would run to the end of the body. I closed the nested claims at the resolving sentence or paragraph break instead, and I did not treat "We now show that" as an opener since it matches none of the listed patterns.
- Rule 5 applied literally labels two substantive steps `setup` because of a parenthetical "(recall that ...)". I followed it literally (PSP1.54, PSP1.57).
- Rule 6 merged the discriminant computation into the preceding step because it says "easily" (PSP1.60).
- Section titles contain `\ref{tm1}` etc.; rendered as "Proof of Theorem 1" per rule 12.
- Rolle, Rouché, Taylor, Gelfond and Liouville are invoked but never stated, so no external nodes for them. `\qed` excluded from proof spans.
- Numbered display equations (1)–(13) were not made `equation` nodes; each lives inside a definition, claim, theorem or step.
- Claim nodes have no `proves` edge (their proofs are nested steps); they link to their proof via `uses`.

All `statement` fields are verbatim copies of source spans (whitespace-collapsed only); no paraphrasing applied to `statement`. `statement_short`, where populated, is LLM-derived compression.
